decisions_2026_10_18: the 1,000 and 10,000 label columns are kept: the same documented command, with only the values of the documented arguments --nlabeled and --size set to the numbers the paper states (maintainer, 2026-10-18)

AUROC is written only to a TensorBoard event file: a generic reader of event files may enter the engine before the lock; otherwise a drawn AUROC claim is INCONCLUSIVE by a limitation of Refute (maintainer, 2026-10-18)

scripts/create_datasets.py is given the datasets cifar10 cifar100 (its own argv, main(argv)): without them it also downloads Tiny ImageNet, which left the inventory by C5, and checks the ImageNet folders

excluded.reason: data_requires_registration_or_terms: ImageNet30 is a subset of ImageNet (README: tar files from the CSI repository); ImageNet is given after login and acceptance of its terms of access (sources/)
data_requires_registration_or_terms: ImageNet100 is a subset of ImageNet-1k (Kaggle copy, License 'Unknown'); the original source requires acceptance of its terms (sources/)
data_license_incompatible (C5): the original source of Tiny ImageNet states no terms (sources/)

excluded.candidate_id: T1/{Only labeled, FixMatch, MTCF, T2T, OpenMatch, IOMatch, SeFOSS}/*/*
excluded.reason: not_produced_by_repository: other methods, run with their official implementations or taken from [56, 47] (section 4); the repository has only ProSub

not_produced_by_repository: every comparison the text states is against another method ("ProSub yields the best results ... in most scenarios"; OpenMatch; FixMatch), which the repository does not produce

main_results_basis: the introduction's contribution: "ProSub, a framework for OSSL achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks" (Table 1); Tables 2 to 4 are analyses and ablations
open_points: The README gives the CIFAR-10 command with 4,000 labels and the CIFAR-100 command with 2,500 labels; the 1,000 and 10,000 columns use the same commands with --nlabeled and create_split --size changed. Kept here as covered by the documented arguments; if the maintainer reads them as variants the instructions do not cover, these 4 cells leave with not_produced_by_repository

AUROC is written only as a TensorBoard summary scalar (prosub_ossl.py lines 512-516); the engine's extraction reads JSON, CSV and the log, so a drawn AUROC claim needs a reader of TensorBoard event files (engine work item) or ends INCONCLUSIVE by Refute's limitation
The seeds of the three runs are not stated; --seed selects the labeled subset only (README note)
